description: We are AstroNova Stellers, a team of 5 passionate and motivated individuals participating in NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. With interests in Full Stack Development, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Data Science, and Software Development, we aim to build an innovative health monitoring solution for astronauts during space missions.
summary:
AstroVital is a daily health companion for astronauts on long Moon and Mars missions, where no doctor is available. It combines seven health signals into one daily status: Stable, Watch, or Act.

Each health signal has its own model: Logistic Regression for sleep, Ridge Regression for stress, Isolation Forest for heart rhythm (HRV), Logistic Regression with PCA for blood chemistry (NASA Inspiration4 and OSD-571 data), PCA for blood metabolites (NASA OSD-431), and a classifier trained on CDC NHANES data for bone risk. Exercise uses a simple rule-based check.

AstroVital compares current values with the astronaut’s own pre-flight baseline. Strong evidence (HRV, blood) is kept separate from weak evidence (sleep, stress, exercise), so weak signals alone never trigger the highest status. Every status comes with reasons and an evidence label.

It is built with FastAPI, scikit-learn, and a React mission-control dashboard with 12 pages.

AstroVital helps astronauts catch the alerts early, on their own.
details:
What it does and how it works:

AstroVital checks seven signals daily: sleep, stress, heart rhythm (HRV), blood chemistry, blood metabolites, bone risk, and exercise. Each signal goes to its own model or rule, and the results are combined into one status: Stable, Watch, or Act. Strong evidence (HRV, blood) and weak evidence (sleep, stress, exercise) are counted separately. Two strong flags, or one strong plus one weak, give Act. Weak flags alone give at most Watch. Missing data is shown as missing and never guessed. Values are compared with the astronaut’s own pre-flight baseline, not only general ranges. Each status shows reasons, an evidence label, and next steps.

Benefits and intended impact:

Astronauts on Moon and Mars missions cannot rely on a nearby doctor. AstroVital helps them notice small changes early, know how much to trust each warning, and know when to contact the mission medical officer. It also gives the medical team a clear view.

Tools and technology:

Frontend: React 18, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Recharts, Framer Motion

Backend: Python, FastAPI, SQLAlchemy (SQLite), Pydantic

ML: scikit-learn (Logistic Regression, Ridge Regression, Isolation Forest, PCA), pandas, numpy

Data: NASA OSDR (Inspiration4, OSD-571, OSD-431), MMASH, CDC NHANES

AI advice: Gemini, with Groq as fallback

Testing: pytest, Vitest

What is creative:

Evidence-aware flagging: the app tells users which warnings are strong and which are weak.

It is honest about model quality. Weak models are labelled weak instead of being hidden.

AI writes only the advice. It never decides the status, and the rules still work if AI is down.

Factors we considered:

Safety: no medication or dosing advice, and red flags always escalate to a flight surgeon.

Small spaceflight datasets: we kept the limits visible.

It is decision support system.
